A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSDBench research. All pages, figures, tables, equations and appendices support comparison, including Appendices A–E in v2 and A–G in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original DSDBench evaluations, self-refinement experiments, component ablations and performance analyses in the main text and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds prompting-strategy evaluations and an agentic repair pilot in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o injection, Llama-3.1-8B generation, snoop tracing, annotation agents and multi-bug construction pipeline remain unchanged. v3 expands their explanation; the new prompting and agentic systems are evaluated alternatives, not revisions to the proposed construction method.

E1.justification: The three source datasets and 1,117-example benchmark remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a limited extension to single-line and unrestricted code-repair tasks on existing single-bug data, beyond the retained localization and downstream DABench coding evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds Zero-shot CoT, One-shot CoT, Self-Refine and Self-Consistency comparisons against direct prompting for three models. Table 12 adds Cursor Agent and OpenHands. These substantially expand the comparison methods, while the original model comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: Appendices F–G introduce alternative prompting procedures and repair protocols: exactly one line changed once, evaluated by pass@1, versus iterative tool-assisted execution without an edit budget, evaluated by pass rate. Existing zero-shot settings and subsets remain; explicit tool prohibitions and all-bugs scoring clarify previously reported evaluations rather than establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 retains the component ablations, error/library breakdowns, bug-count and hop analyses, and case study. It adds systematic prompting-strategy sensitivity analysis across three models and an agentic pilot examining how constrained versus unrestricted repair affects success.

E5.justification: Dataset dispersion statistics and performance-reporting practices are unchanged. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Self-Consistency is evaluated as an inference strategy, not reported as an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing result tables and figures retain their values. New Table 11 reports, for example, GPT-4o Self-Consistency cause/effect accuracies of 37.5/34.4 versus direct prompting's 35.4/31.2. Table 12 adds Cursor/OpenHands single-attempt repair scores of 48.9/18.6 and unrestricted rates of approximately 100/41.7. Repair and localization results use different tasks and metrics.

T1.justification: Formal task tuples, dataset notation and scoring equations are retained. The expanded hop discussion clarifies the existing distinction between identical and different cause/effect lines; it introduces no different mathematical property, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain. The abstract and introduction now emphasize non-expert scripting and interpreter-visible crashes, and explicitly claim a generation-versus-understanding gap, refining the earlier broad framing around difficult data-science debugging.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of synthetic-bug realism, injection bias, crash-only coverage and masking interactions between bugs. It also interprets prompting gains and attributes agentic repair outcomes to generation alignment and broad rewriting that can obscure localization weaknesses. The original standalone limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents tool/execution restrictions and all-bugs scoring, adds a semantic-message scoring example, and identifies the Cursor backend and OpenHands cloud interface. Existing prompts and code-access information remain. The full scoring rubric promised in Section 3.2 is absent from Appendix D, and new prompting/sampling details remain limited.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Related Work section remain essentially unchanged. New abstract/introduction passages distinguish non-expert data-science scripting from SWE-bench's repository-level patch evaluation, while Appendix G positions localization as complementary to repair pass rates.

P1.justification: The abstract, error-injection description, task definition, metric explanation and self-debugging narrative receive substantial rewrites. v3 adds rationale and scope subheadings, Appendices F–G and acknowledgments, and corrects the self-debugging discussion's reference from Table 4 to Figure 4.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 11–12 and redistributes existing tables and figures across pages and columns. Figures 1–13 and Tables 1–10 retain their content and basic display structure; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies scope and scoring and adds potentially useful experiments. However, Table 11's Qwen baseline of 26.0/26.0 conflicts with Table 9's 25.0/30.2, and Table 12 uses different repair and localization metrics to support a generation advantage. Missing prompting/sampling details and the absent promised scoring rubric further limit assessment. These unresolved problems weaken the new interpretations, so the PDFs do not establish whether the added clarity and evidence produce a net quality improvement.
